verses.zh: 扫罗追赶非利士人回来，有人告诉他说：「大卫在隐・基底的旷野。」
verses.en: (24:2) When Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “Look, David is in the desert of En Gedi.”

verses.zh: 扫罗就从以色列人中挑选三千精兵，率领他们往野羊的磐石去，寻索大卫和跟随他的人。
verses.en: So Saul took 3,000 select men from all Israel and went to find[NOTE:1] David and his men in the region of[NOTE:2] the rocks of the mountain goats.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “the region of the Rocks of the Mountain Goats,” if this expression is understood as a place name (cf. NASB, NIV, NRSV, TEV, CEV).

verses.zh: 到了路旁的羊圈，在那里有洞，扫罗进去大解。大卫和跟随他的人正藏在洞里的深处。
verses.en: He came to the sheepfolds by the road, where there was a cave. Saul went into it to relieve himself.[NOTE:1] Now David and his men were sitting in the recesses of the cave.
notes: Heb “to cover his feet,” an idiom (euphemism) for relieving oneself (cf. NAB “to ease nature”).

verses.zh: 跟随的人对大卫说：「耶和华曾应许你说：『我要将你的仇敌交在你手里，你可以任意待他。』如今时候到了！」大卫就起来，悄悄地割下扫罗外袍的衣襟。
verses.en: David’s men said to him, “This is the day about which the Lord said to you, ‘I will give your enemy into your hand, and you can do to him whatever seems appropriate to you.’”[NOTE:1] So David got up and quietly cut off an edge of Saul’s robe.

verses.zh: 随后大卫心中自责，因为割下扫罗的衣襟；
verses.en: Afterward David’s conscience bothered him[NOTE:1] because he had cut off an edge of Saul’s robe.
notes: Heb “the heart of David struck him.”

verses.zh: 对跟随他的人说：「我的主乃是耶和华的受膏者，我在耶和华面前万不敢伸手害他，因他是耶和华的受膏者。」
verses.en: He said to his men, “May the Lord keep me far away from doing such a thing to my lord, who is the Lord’s chosen one,[NOTE:1] by extending my hand against him. After all,[NOTE:2] he is the Lord’s chosen one.”
notes: Heb “anointed.” Also at the end of this verse.

verses.zh: 大卫用这话拦住跟随他的人，不容他们起来害扫罗。扫罗起来，从洞里出去行路。
verses.en: David restrained his men with these words and did not allow them to rise up against Saul. Then Saul left the cave and started down[NOTE:1] the road.

verses.zh: 随后大卫也起来，从洞里出去，呼叫扫罗说：「我主，我王！」扫罗回头观看，大卫就屈身、脸伏于地下拜。
verses.en: Afterward David got up and went out of the cave. He called out to Saul, “My lord, O king!” When Saul looked behind him, David kneeled down and bowed with his face to the ground.

verses.zh: 大卫对扫罗说：「你为何听信人的谗言，说大卫想要害你呢？
verses.en: David said to Saul, “Why do you pay attention when men say, ‘David is seeking to do you harm’?

verses.zh: 今日你亲眼看见在洞中，耶和华将你交在我手里；有人叫我杀你，我却爱惜你，说：『我不敢伸手害我的主，因为他是耶和华的受膏者。』
verses.en: Today your own eyes see how the Lord delivered you—this very day—into my hands in the cave. Some told me to kill you, but I had pity[NOTE:1] on you and said, ‘I will not extend my hand against my lord, for he is the Lord’s chosen one.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “it had pity,” apparently with the understood subject being “my eye,” in accordance with a common expression.

verses.zh: 我父啊，看看你外袍的衣襟在我手中。我割下你的衣襟，没有杀你；你由此可以知道我没有恶意叛逆你。你虽然猎取我的命，我却没有得罪你。
verses.en: Look, my father, and see the edge of your robe in my hand! When I cut off the edge of your robe, I didn’t kill you. So realize and understand that I am not planning[NOTE:1] evil or rebellion. Even though I have not sinned against you, you are waiting in ambush to take my life.
notes: Heb “there is not in my hand.”

verses.zh: 愿耶和华在你我中间判断是非，在你身上为我伸冤，我却不亲手加害于你。
verses.en: May the Lord judge between the two of us, and may the Lord vindicate me over you, but my hand will not be against you.

verses.zh: 古人有句俗语说：『恶事出于恶人。』我却不亲手加害于你。
verses.en: It’s like the old proverb says: ‘From evil people evil proceeds.’ But my hand will not be against you.

verses.zh: 以色列王出来要寻找谁呢？追赶谁呢？不过追赶一条死狗，一个虼蚤就是了。
verses.en: Who has the king of Israel come out after? Who is it that you are pursuing? A dead dog? A single flea?

verses.zh: 愿耶和华在你我中间施行审判，断定是非，并且鉴察，为我伸冤，救我脱离你的手。」
verses.en: May the Lord be our judge and arbiter. May he see and arbitrate my case and deliver me from your hands.”

verses.zh: 大卫向扫罗说完这话，扫罗说：「我儿大卫，这是你的声音吗？」就放声大哭，
verses.en: When David finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said, “Is that your voice, my son David?” Then Saul wept loudly.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 对大卫说：「你比我公义；因为你以善待我，我却以恶待你。
verses.en: He said to David, “You are more innocent[NOTE:1] than I, for you have treated me well, even though I have tried to harm you.
notes: Or “righteous” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NAB “you are in the right”; NLT “are a better man than I am.”

verses.zh: 你今日显明是以善待我；因为耶和华将我交在你手里，你却没有杀我。
verses.en: You have explained today how you have treated me well. The Lord delivered me into your hand, but you did not kill me.

verses.zh: 人若遇见仇敌，岂肯放他平安无事地去呢？愿耶和华因你今日向我所行的，以善报你。
verses.en: Now if a man finds his enemy, does he send him on his way in good shape? May the Lord repay you with good this day for what you have done to me.

verses.zh: 我也知道你必要作王，以色列的国必坚立在你手里。
verses.en: Now look, I realize that you will in fact be king and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands.

verses.zh: 现在你要指着耶和华向我起誓，不剪除我的后裔，在我父家不灭没我的名。」
verses.en: So now swear to me in the Lord’s name[NOTE:1] that you will not kill[NOTE:2] my descendants after me or destroy my name from the house of my father.”

verses.zh: 于是大卫向扫罗起誓，扫罗就回家去；大卫和跟随他的人上山寨去了。
verses.en: David promised Saul this on oath.[NOTE:1] Then Saul went to his house, and David and his men went up to the stronghold.
notes: Heb “and David swore an oath to Saul.”

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 24:1-7

1Now when Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, saying, "Behold, David is
in the wilderness of Engedi." 2Then Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and
went to seek David and his men in front of the Rocks of the Wild Goats. 3He came to the
sheepfolds on the way, where there was a cave; and Saul went in to relieve himself. Now David and his men
were sitting in the inner recesses of the cave. 4The men of David said to him, "Behold, this is
the day of which the Lord said to you, 'Behold; I am about to give your enemy
into your hand, and you shall do to him as it seems good to you.'" Then David arose and cut off the edge of
Saul's robe secretly. 5It came about afterward that David's conscience bothered him because
he had cut off the edge of Saul's robe. 6So he said to his men, "Far be it from me because of
the Lord that I should do this thing to my lord, the Lord's
anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, since he is the Lord's anointed."
7David persuaded his men with these words and did not allow them to rise up against Saul. And
Saul arose, left the cave, and went on his way.

24:2 "chosen men" These were his best, most loyal soldiers, probably Benjamites. Notice he takes 3,000 to
confront David's 600.

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA
"the Rocks of the Wild Goats"

NJB, REB
"the rocks of Mountain Goats"

LXX
"Sadaiem"

Peshitta
"the mountains of the wild goats"

This must have been somewhere close to Engedi (lit. "spring of wild goats"). The Rift Valley
rises quickly to the hill country of Judea.

24:3 "relieve himself" This (BDB 696, KB 754, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
is literally "cover his feet." several times in the OT "feet" are a euphemism for

- male genitals (cf. Exod. 4:25; Jdgs. 3:24; Ruth 3:4,7,8,14; Isa. 7:20)

- female genitalia (cf. Deut. 28:57; Ezek. 16:25)

- possibly angelic genitalia (cf. Isa. 6:2)

NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 1048, mentions that in 2 Kgs. 18:27 and Isa. 18:27; 36:12, where urine is called "water of feet."

24:4 David spares Saul's life but takes the opportunity to try to show him that he was not his enemy (vv. 8-15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: "the sons of God" in
GENESIS 6

▣ "enemy" The MT has a PLURAL Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE,
but the Masoretic scholars suggested a SINGULAR (BDB 33, KB 38).

▣ David's men take Saul's entering the cave as a sign YHWH was delivering him to David, but this was
not the case. Be careful of random circumstances being interpreted as the will of God! Revelation and
spiritual discernment, not circumstances, must guide our lives!

24:5 "David's conscience bothered him" This is literally "David's heart smote him" (BDB 645, KB 697, Hiphil
IMPERFECT with waw). This same imagery is used of David again in 2 Sam. 24:10. David had a soft
heart toward God.

▣

NASB
"the edge"

NKJV, NRSV
"a corner"

TEV, REB
"a piece"

NJB
"the border"

JPSOA
"the corner"

LXX
"the wing"

Peshitta
"the skirt"

The MT has the FEMININE NOUN (BDB 489, KB 486), which denotes the end of a
garment (i.e., Saul's royal robe). The same word occurs for Samuel's priestly robe in 1 Sam. 15:27. It is used of a common
robe in Num. 15:38; Deut. 22:12.

24:6 David felt that Saul was still in a sense YHWH's chosen king (lit. anointed). Saul's removal must be an act of
God, not David.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "ANOINTING" IN THE BIBLE

24:7

"persuaded"

"restrained"

NRSV
"scolded"

TEV
"convinced"

REB
"reproved"

JPSOA
"said to his men"

The MT has the strong VERB (BDB 1042, KB 1608, Piel
IMPERFECT with waw) which means "divide," "cleave," "tear in pieces." BDB comments that this
is too strong in meaning for this context and suggests a textual error for the word "restrains."

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 24:8-15

8Now afterward David arose and went out of the cave and called after Saul, saying, "My lord the
king!" And when Saul looked behind him, David bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.
9David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of men, saying, 'Behold, David seeks to
harm you'? 10Behold, this day your eyes have seen that the Lord
had given you today into my hand in the cave, and some said to kill you, but my eye had pity on you; and I
said, 'I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is the Lord's anointed.'
11Now, my father, see! Indeed, see the edge of your robe in my hand! For in that I cut off the
edge of your robe and did not kill you, know and perceive that there is no evil or rebellion in my hands, and
I have not sinned against you, though you are lying in wait for my life to take it. 12May the
Lord judge between you and me, and may the Lord
avenge me on you; but my hand shall not be against you. 13As the proverb of the ancients says,
'Out of the wicked comes forth wickedness'; but my hand shall not be against you. 14After whom
has the king of Israel come out? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog, a single flea? 15The
Lord therefore be judge and decide between you and me; and may He see and
plead my cause and deliver me from your hand."

24:8 David showed humility and honor to Saul.

- called him "My lord the king," v. 8

- bowed his face to the ground, v. 8

- prostrated himself, v. 8

- called him "father" (respectful imagery), v. 11

- calls himself

- a dead dog, v. 14

- a single flea, v. 14

24:9 Saul had been given bad advice from

- his counselors

- Doeg

- the evil spirit from the Lord

- military, family leaders

24:11 Notice the imperatives.

- "see" ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal

- "see" ‒ same as #1 (repeated for emphasis)

- "know" ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal

- "perceive" ‒ lit. "see," same as #1,2

David claims he has not acted militantly against Saul.

- no evil

- no rebellion

- no sin

24:12 "May the Lord judge between you and me" This is a Qal
IMPERFECT VERB used in a JUSSIVE sense (BDB 1047, KB 1622).

Even though the next VERB is a PERFECT, it seems to be used also
in a JUSSIVE sense (as in v. 15).

24:13 David is promising that he will not attack Saul (vv. 12-13). He is not the proverbial "wicked
person" (BDB 957), but a loyal subject.

24:14 This is common ANE imagery of insignificance.

24:15 When YHWH judges, David is convinced He will.

- YHWH will see (i.e., know) ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal JUSSIVE

- YHWH will defend David (lit. "plead my cause") ‒ BDB 936, KB 1224, Qal JUSSIVE

- YHWH will deliver ‒ BDB 1047, KB 1622, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 24:16-22

16When David had finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said, "Is this your voice, my son
David?" Then Saul lifted up his voice and wept. 17He said to David, "You are more righteous than
I; for you have dealt well with me, while I have dealt wickedly with you. 18You have declared today
that you have done good to me, that the Lord delivered me into your hand and
yet you did not kill me. 19For if a man finds his enemy, will he let him go away safely? May the
Lord therefore reward you with good in return for what you have done to me this
day. 20Now, behold, I know that you will surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be
established in your hand. 21So now swear to me by the Lord that
you will not cut off my descendants after me and that you will not destroy my name from my father's household."
22David swore to Saul. And Saul went to his home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.

24:16-22 This paragraph is so sad to me. The mental illness of Saul is clearly revealed in his

- past acts (trying to kill David)

- current humility

- calls David "my son," v. 16

- he wept, v. 16

- you are more righteous than I, v. 17; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS.

- admitted his wickedness against David, v. 17

- David's mercy to him, vv. 18-19

24:17 "while I" This is an intensified structure that emphasizes the contrast between Saul's actions and
David's actions. This relates back to v. 12. YHWH will judge between these two anointed leaders!

24:20 What a shocking admission! This is what Jonathan had asserted in 1 Sam. 23:17. Saul knew YHWH's will
but chose to try to alter it!

▣ "you shall surely be king" This is the intensified construction of an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and an IMPERFECT VERB of the same root (BDB 573, KB 590).

24:21 Saul asked David not to kill his family and cut off his name, as Jonathan had asked in 1 Sam. 20;15.
This death to all relatives was common in the ANE when kingship changed (cf. Jdgs. 9:5; 1 Kgs. 15:29; 16:11; 2 Kgs. 10:1-17; 11:1).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why was David "heart struck" because he cut Saul's robe?

- How did David's men interpret Saul being alone in the cave?

- How does David try to show he holds no ill will against Saul?

- What are the implications of v. 20?
